whatis.intro: Safety stock is the extra stock you hold for days that do not go to plan. A busier day or a late truck draws on it. It is sized from how much demand and lead time swing, not from the averages alone. Here that comes to 229 cases.

cards.title: How far demand and lead time stray
cards.body: How far demand and lead time stray from their averages. Two lines that both sell 120 cases a day can need very different buffers.
cards.alt: Plus sign, for how far demand and lead time stray

cards.title: Partial deliveries are not in it
cards.body: Supplier shorts. A truck that arrives late is in the formula, but one that arrives with part of the order is not. A partial delivery eats the buffer without warning.
cards.alt: Minus sign, for a supplier delivery that arrives short

cards.title: A swing with names on it
cards.body: For a distributor, the 35 case swing can trace back to a few accounts that order big and irregularly. Part of the buffer is paying for their pattern.
cards.alt: Storefront, for the accounts behind the demand swing

who.h2: Who uses a safety stock calculator
who.intro: Inventory planners at distributors carrying dated and dry lines use it to size the buffer under each one. Anyone who decides how much spare stock to keep, or defends that call in cash, should run it.

look.h2: How a safety stock buffer gets sized wrong
look.intro: The formula does the hard part. The swings you feed it decide the answer, so get them right before cash goes into a buffer.

steps.title: A swing measured day by day
steps.body: The 35 case swing is how far one day strays from 120. Work it out from weekly totals divided by seven and it comes out too small.

steps.title: Demand, not shipments
steps.body: In a week you ran short, shipments look calmer than what accounts asked for. Build the swing from orders, or the short weeks shrink the buffer meant to cover them.

steps.title: What 95% really promises
steps.body: It means a 5.0% chance of running out in each restock cycle. It is not a 95% fill rate, which counts the cases you ship.

vos.h2: Where VOS fits in your buffer
vos.h3: The swing starts with what each account orders
vos.body: VOS does not size your buffer or forecast demand. It keeps a record to check your swing against: each order placed by voice in the VOS app, by account and time.
